findings.F1: The whole in-stretch deficit sits in the gap from one bar's close to the next bar's open: that gap averages -0.99% on in-stretch bars against -0.0007% out of stretch, while the next bar's open-to-close move is +0.11% in-stretch against -0.03% out, so the -0.86% in-stretch mean next-bar return (vs -0.03% out, Welch t -4.14) comes from a near-constant -1% step between bars and not from intraday trading.
findings.F2: The negative drift is uniform across signal strength rather than growing with it: next-bar means are -0.87%, -0.90%, -0.77% and -0.96% for forecast bins 0-5, 5-10, 10-15 and 15-20, all against -0.03% at forecast 0, with up-shares of 23-31% against 48%.
findings.F3: Every one of the 5 up-cross stretches loses, with no exception by window: w1_1 -20.9% cumulative over 13 bars, w4_2 -44.7% over 82, w5_1 -72.9% over 122, w6_1 -10.4% over 11 and w6_3 -34.2% over 62, with up-shares between 18% and 35%.
findings.F4: Within each window that has both states, in-stretch bars trail out-of-stretch bars: w1 -1.76% vs -0.07% (t -2.33), w4 -0.68% vs +0.94% (t -3.26) and w6 -0.70% vs +0.62% (t -3.44); out-of-stretch bars in w4 and w6 even rise more often than not (59% and 54% up).
findings.F5: The reversal does not fade with time spent above the long average: in-stretch next-bar means are -0.96% in the first 10 bars of a stretch, -1.31% at bars 10-30, -0.32% at bars 30-60 and -1.08% at bars 60-120, while out-of-stretch bars stay between -0.26% and +0.29% at every age.
findings.F6: The in-stretch loss is a shifted centre rather than a fat tail: the in-stretch median is -1.06% against -0.06% out, the 75th percentile is +0.23% against +1.36%, and in-stretch bars are calmer, with a 3.4% next-bar high-low range against 4.4%.
findings.F7: Daily persistence is absent in both states: the correlation of a bar's return with the next one is -0.035 in-stretch and +0.006 out of stretch, and in-stretch bars lose about the same after an up bar (-0.94%) as after a down bar (-0.87%).
findings.F8: The effect is present on every weekday: in-stretch next-bar means run from -0.15% on Monday to -1.75% on Wednesday, against out-of-stretch means between -0.23% and +0.23%.
findings.F9: The coin fell in every window (-17.9% to -72.9%) and the rejection rests on 2023, where 277 in-stretch bars averaged -0.85% against +0.76% for 85 out-of-stretch bars (t -5.96); 2022 adds only 13 in-stretch bars (-1.76% vs -0.22%, t -2.29).
findings.F10: The book records no trades, yet its value moves in four windows: +24.9% in w4 and +26.0% in w6 while the coin lost about 22% in each, and -8.1% in w1 and -8.9% in w5 against coin losses of -30.8% and -72.9%.

ideas.idea: While BTC's 50-day SMA sits above its 200-day SMA, the next daily bar's open-to-close move is positive on average. Any loss in that stretch comes from the step between one bar's close and the next bar's open, not from trading within the bar.
ideas.consequence: In an up-regime, judge the trend's persistence by the open-to-close move, not close-to-close returns, because the -1% step at the bar boundary is probably a data shift (the plan carries a "minus1pct" tag, and the coin falls throughout 2023) rather than market behaviour.
ideas.name: up-regime intrabar drift positive
